member.name: T:PerformanceStatistics.Internal.DeltaSampler`2
member.summary:
Turns a monotonically increasing raw sample (CPU ticks, cumulative disk operations, process CPU time) into a rate computed over the interval between two reads. Shared by every platform so that rate metrics behave identically on Windows, Linux, and macOS:
The first read waits until the minimum interval has elapsed since the baseline sample, so a one-shot caller still receives a real value instead of zero.
Reads closer together than the minimum interval return the previously computed value instead of resetting the baseline, so reading related properties back-to-back is consistent.
When a progress predicate is supplied and the raw counters have not advanced (macOS publishes host CPU ticks in bursts, sometimes nearly a second apart), the baseline is kept and the previous value is returned; the first read polls until the counters advance or elapses.
Timing uses , which is monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock changes.
Thread-safe.

member.name: T:PerformanceStatistics.Windows.WindowsSystemCounters
member.summary:
Windows system counters.
CPU: GetSystemTimes deltas (independent of the localized performance counter names).
Memory: GlobalMemoryStatusEx available physical memory.
Disk operations: cumulative raw values of the PhysicalDisk(_Total) "Disk Reads/sec" and "Disk Writes/sec" counters.
Disk queues: PhysicalDisk(_Total) "Avg. Disk Read/Write Queue Length", averaged since the previous read (the first read may be 0).
Disk space: fixed drives.
Performance counters are created on first use and reused; if they are unavailable (disabled or corrupted counter registry), the disk operation and queue properties return null.
